r.method: Loaded the l29 prims cache and, for each candidate, dumped every wall / door / glazing item and nested block in a window around it (wall hatch loops, A-WALL line ends, door blocks with their children: frames A-DOOR-FRAM, leaf lines A-DOOR-HDLN, arcs, Door-Opening jambs A-DETL-MEDM), then rendered the spot at 1.5-3 m scale to confirm. Hinged doors in the links and in the main file were measured as the leaf extents between the frame/jamb pieces (wall gap minus 0.04-0.06 frame on each side); glass doors between the glazed panels; double doors between the jambs; lift and sliding doors between frames / wall ends. Then scanned the whole floor: all door/window INSERT families, multi-loop wall hatches (wall pieces split by an opening) and a ray scan from every short wall-end face (0.55-2.7 m to the next wall), plus four quadrant renders, to find openings no candidate covers (extraFinds). Only the drawing and the supplied tools were used. Result also written to audit.json in the output folder.

r.method: Pictures first, then numbers. For each of the 30 candidates I rendered a 3 x 3 m view (--grid 0.25 --inserts, a/b marks; L29-Cnn.png), plus four context renders (ctx_NW, ctx_N, ctx_W, ctx_SW) to understand rooms, corridors and what each gap separates. I then listed the primitives of prims.pkl around every place (A-WALL wall ends, A-DOOR / A-DOOR-FRAM jamb boxes, A-DOOR-HDLN header lines, A-DETL-GENF jamb profiles and leaves, A-DETL-GENF-HDLN swing arcs, A-DETL-MEDM jambs, A-GLAZ-CURT panel ends, A-FLOR threshold lines, block names and insert points) and measured the clear opening between jamb inner faces (narrowest through the wall depth) for hinged / double / sliding doors, between the wall ends or Door-Opening jamb lines for doorless passages, and the wall centre line for the cross coordinate. Final a/b were re-rendered with marks on the inner jamb faces (Cnn_final.png, X_*.png). Rules used: a gap counts as an opening only if a wall line with wall on both sides is interrupted at doorway scale or a door / Door-Opening / glass door block stands there; open corridor or lobby ends, wall ends facing a far wall, dead-end cavities, equipment recesses, fins and glass partition bays are not openings. Most door candidates were wall-end to wall-end (8-12 cm wider than the clear opening), so a/b and width differ from the candidate segments. extraFinds lists doors, Door-Openings, one stair-hall gap, a lift opening and optional cubicle doors seen next to the candidates.

r.method: Rendered every candidate (3 x 3 m or larger zoom with 0.25 m grid, own layer-coloured renderer: wall fills, glazing, door layers, hidden lines, candidate overlay) and read the primitives in prims.pkl around it: A-WALL lines and hatches for wall ends, A-DOOR / A-DOOR-FRAM / A-DOOR-HDLN for jambs, leaves and heads of the door blocks (top level and nested in the links), A-DETL-GENF-HDLN swing arcs, A-DETL closure lines, A-DETL-MEDM jambs, A-GENM stall blocks. Clear openings are the narrowest gap between frame jamb inner faces (hinged / sliding) or between wall ends (passages), on the wall centre line. r.method: Pictures first: rendered each of the 43 candidates with render.py (3.2 m window or wider, grid 0.25, --inserts, a/b marks) and read every image, plus nine wider context renders (north block, east facade, SE glass box, west corridor, x=18 wall, WC lobby, service corridor, stall rooms). Then confirmed numbers from prims.pkl: A-WALL end faces, A-DOOR / A-DOOR-FRAM jamb lines of each door block, A-DETL span lines (a set of consecutive-handle lines that bridge doors, lift gaps, the stair entrance and the C41/C32 gaps), the dashed A-DETL header lines, and the A-GENM cubicle boxes. Rules: doors measured between the inner faces of the frame/jamb lines (narrowest through the wall depth) and placed on the wall centre line (the door insert coordinate); sliding doors between the frames; passages between wall end faces. Facade fins, caps, glass partitions and glazed boxes are not openings; segments that only cross a corridor, aisle or room between two wall faces, or run from a free wall end to a non-wall line, are not openings. Doorless gaps between collinear wall ends with jamb-like returns and a closing line (C32, C41) are passages; a gap with no returns or closing line but a clear service-room entrance (C37) is an optional passage. Also listed every door block, lift gap, stair entrance and cubicle door that no candidate covers (extraFinds).

r.method: Read tower.json with Python and kept floor tower:L29 (37 entries: 27 non-optional, 10 optional). r.method: Read only tower.json (L30 entries) and the L30 prims.pkl via tools/prims.py. For each entry I located the opening from the key's coordinates, then listed with small helper scripts (h.py in the output folder: dump / cross / byh) every segment crossing the wall band at the opening: A-DOOR, A-DOOR-FRAM, A-DOOR-HDLN, A-DETL-MEDM and the A-DETL-GENF jamb details, A-WALL and A-WALL-PATT hatch loops and end lines, S-COLS, the A-GENM stall-post hatches, and the complete content of each door block by DXF handle. Clear opening per the convention: hinged doors = inner faces of the frame jambs, taking the narrowest face where the jamb profile is stepped; sliders / pocket doors = inner faces of the frames drawn between the wall ends; passages and the Door-Opening / lift-opening families = narrowest gap between wall ends or family jamb returns through the wall thickness; cubicle doors = inner faces of the two door posts; window = glass between the end mullion faces. Compared a and b with the key along the wall axis (millimetre values from the geometry); ok only when both ends are < 5.0 cm off; corrected ends are put on the key's own centre line and keep its a/b order. I rendered the openings with tools/render.py (0.1 m grid) and looked at the plan of 23 of the 38 (every door family, slider type and passage type: W-05, 06/07, 08, 09, 10, 11, 12, 14, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 26, 27, 32; E-02, 03, 07, 08, 11); for the other entries (same families: native DOOR_SWING blocks, stall blocks, plain lift gaps) I relied on the exact primitives listed by block handle. Finally I generated an annotated figure for every entry (orange dashed = key a / b, green = clear opening a / b): 38 PNGs, one per L30 key entry.
